div.l: He rode but homely . in a medly cote .
Girt with a seynt of silk . with barris smale .
Of his a raye . tell I no lenger tale .
A Frankeleyn . was in his companye .
White was his berde . as is the daies eye .
Of his complexion . he was sangwyne .
Well loued he bi the morow . a sop in wyne .
To lyuen in delite . euyr was hys wone .
For he was . epitures owne sone .
That heelde opynyon . that pleyn delite .
Was verray . felicite ꝑperfite .
An housholder . ⁊and that a gret was he .
Seynt Iulian . he was in his Cuntre .
His breed his ale . was alweye after oon .
A bettyr enuyned man . was nowher noon .
With oute bake mete . was neuer his hous .
Of fysch ⁊and flesch . ⁊and that so plenteuous .
It snewed in his hous . of mete ⁊and drynke .
Of all deyntes . that men cowde thenke .
After / the sondry sesons . of the yere .
So chaūnged he his mete . ⁊and his sopere .
Full many a fat partriche . had he in mewe
And many a breme . ⁊and many a pike in stewe .
Wo was his cook . but his sauce were .
Poynant ⁊and scharp . ⁊and redy all his gere .
His table dormant . in his halle alway .
Stood redy coủered . all the long day .
At sessions . there was he lorde ⁊and sire .
Full ofte tyme . he was knyght of þe schire .
An anlas . ⁊and a gipser all of silk .
Heeng at his gyrdell . white as morne mylk .
A schereue had he ben . ⁊and acoronorur .
Was nowher . suche a worthi vauasorur .
An haberdascher . ⁊and a Carpynter .
A Webbe . A dyer . ⁊and a Tapycer .
And thei were clothed . alle in oo lyuere .
Of a solempne . ⁊and a grete fraternyte .
Full fresch ⁊and newe . here gere piked was .
Here knyues . were noght chapid with bras .
But all with siluer / . wrought full clene ⁊and well .
Here gurthels . ⁊and here powches eủerydell .
Well semed eche of hem . a fayre burgeys .
To sitten in a yeldehalle . on a deys .
Eủerych . for the wisdam that he can .
Was schaply . for to ben an Alderman.
For catell thei had y nowe . ⁊and rente .
And eke here wyues . wolde it well assente . /
